parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: A sample contains three different types of atom: $^{40}_{18}\text{Ar}$, $^{40}_{19}\text{K}$ and $^{40}_{20}\text{Ca}$.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State fully, in terms of the numbers of subatomic particles, what these three atoms have in common.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State fully, in terms of the numbers of **all** subatomic particles, how these three atoms **differ** from each other.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A sample of sulfur contains only two isotopes, $^{32}\text{S}$ and $^{34}\text{S}$. The relative atomic mass of this sample is 32.09.

| isotope | isotopic mass |
| :--- | :--- |
| $^{32}\text{S}$ | 32.0 |
| $^{34}\text{S}$ | 34.0 |

Calculate the percentage abundance of the isotopes present in this sample.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The electronic configuration of a sulfur atom is $1s^22s^22p^63s^23p^4$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Identify which orbital in a sulfur atom has the lowest energy.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Sketch the shape of a p orbital.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
During the process of ionisation a sulfur atom loses an electron.

$$\text{S(g)} \rightarrow \text{S}^+\text{(g)} + \text{e}^- \quad \Delta H = 1000\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Identify the orbital from which this electron is removed. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
Complete the diagram to show the arrangement of electrons within the third shell of a phosphorus atom.


{{figure:visual_auto_01.png}}

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the first ionisation energy of sulfur is less than that of phosphorus.
